three-word-day.title: Three-word day
three-word-day.text: Describe your day in exactly three words. Everyone votes on the most dramatic description. Its author gives out one sip.

tiny-sales-pitch.title: An offer you can refuse
tiny-sales-pitch.text: Pick an ordinary object nearby and give it a ten-second sales pitch. If anyone wants to buy it, give out one sip. Otherwise, take one.

unpopular-snack.title: Snack court
unpopular-snack.text: Defend an unpopular food combination. The table votes: delicious or disaster? Join the smaller group for one sip.

soundtrack.title: Your entrance music
soundtrack.text: Choose the song that should play whenever you enter a room. The player on your left chooses your entrance pose. Perform the pose or take one sip.

bad-superpower.title: Super, probably
bad-superpower.text: Invent a useless superpower. The player on your right explains how it could save the world. If the table buys the explanation, you both give out one sip.

two-second-logo.title: Air designer
two-second-logo.text: Draw a familiar logo in the air with one finger. The first person to name it gives out one sip. Nobody gets it? Take one sip.

imaginary-holiday.title: National what day?
imaginary-holiday.text: Invent a holiday and its strangest tradition. Everyone who would celebrate it raises a hand. If nobody volunteers, take one sip.

table-awards.title: And the award goes to…
table-awards.text: Give the player on your left a made-up award for something kind or funny. They give a five-second acceptance speech, then choose someone to take one sip.

odd-one-out.title: Three things
odd-one-out.text: Name three things. The next player has ten seconds to explain something they all have in common. A convincing answer earns them one sip to give away; otherwise they take one.

five-things.title: Packing light
five-things.text: Name five things you would take to a deserted island, without using anything another player says first. The table supplies distractions. Pause for five seconds and take one sip.

backwards-introduction.title: Wrong answers welcome
backwards-introduction.text: The player on your right asks you three simple questions. Give a different, obviously wrong answer each time. Accidentally tell the truth? Take one sip.

mystery-object.title: Mystery object
mystery-object.text: Choose something you can see. Describe it without its name, colour, or usual purpose. The first person to guess it gives out one sip.

group-photo-title.title: Name the album
group-photo-title.text: If tonight were an album, what would its title be? Everyone suggests one. The table’s favourite gives out one sip.

tiny-debate.title: Very serious debate
tiny-debate.text: You and the player on your left each get ten seconds: which is better, an extra hour of sleep or an extra hour of free time? Everyone else votes. The losing side takes one sip; with two players, call it a draw.

holiday-planner.title: Mystery holiday
holiday-planner.text: Describe a real place you want to visit using only three clues. The first person to guess it gives out one sip. Reveal the answer if nobody knows it.

silent-movie.title: Silent cinema
silent-movie.text: Act out making your favourite meal without speaking. You have twenty seconds. Whoever guesses first gives out one sip; no correct guesses means you take one.

table-telepathy.title: Same wavelength
table-telepathy.text: Choose another player. On the count of three, each name a fruit. Match and give out one sip each. Miss and simply try again once.

museum-piece.title: Museum of ordinary things
museum-piece.text: Present something nearby as a priceless museum exhibit. Explain its mysterious history in two sentences. The first player to laugh takes one sip.

new-constellation.title: Written in the stars
new-constellation.text: Invent a constellation named after someone at the table. Describe its shape and the legend behind it. That player gives out one sip.

restaurant-review.title: Five-star nonsense
restaurant-review.text: Review an imaginary restaurant where the food is great but everything else is bizarre. Finish with a star rating. The table’s harshest critic takes one sip.

animal-interview.title: A word with the penguin
animal-interview.text: The player on your right interviews you as an animal they choose. Answer two questions in character. Break character and take one sip.

one-word-story.title: Once upon a table
one-word-story.text: Build a story around the table, one word per player. After one complete circle, you must give the story a title. Anyone who laughs during their word takes one sip.

terrible-invention.title: Patent pending
terrible-invention.text: Invent a product that solves a very minor problem in a ridiculous way. The next player names it. Everyone who would use it takes one sip.

time-traveller.title: Welcome to the future
time-traveller.text: Explain a smartphone to a visitor from two hundred years ago without using the words phone, internet, or computer. Let another player choose a sip for you if you slip up.

fake-fact.title: Completely unverified
fake-fact.text: Make up a harmless, obviously silly fact about an everyday object. Another player delivers it like a documentary narrator. First to laugh takes one sip.

perfect-pair.title: Better together
perfect-pair.text: Name two things that belong together. The next player replaces one with something unexpected and explains why the new pair works. The table decides who gives out one sip.

mini-mime.title: Tiny job interview
mini-mime.text: Mime a job using only your hands. The first player to guess the job gives out one sip. After twenty seconds, reveal it and move on.

opening-credits.title: Tonight, starring…
opening-credits.text: Introduce the table as the cast of a fictional show. Give each player a character name. The player on your left chooses someone to take one sip.

weather-report.title: Party forecast
weather-report.text: Deliver a ten-second weather forecast for the mood at the table. Include one dramatic prediction. Anyone who interrupts takes one sip.

first-impression.title: A pleasant surprise
first-impression.text: Tell someone at the table one nice thing you noticed about them. Both of you choose a third player for a shared toast; with two players, toast each other.

rhythm-copy.title: Tabletop orchestra
rhythm-copy.text: Tap a short rhythm. The player on your left copies it and adds one beat. Continue once around the table. The first missed beat costs one sip.

shared-toast.title: Cheers to that
shared-toast.text: Name one small thing worth celebrating today. Everyone may add their own. Raise a glass together and take a sip if you like.

royal-requests.title: Royal requests
royal-requests.text: Begin every request to another player with “Your Majesty.” Forget the royal treatment and take one sip.

third-person.title: Your own narrator
third-person.text: Speak about yourself in the third person. Slip back to “I” or “me” and take one sip.

news-anchor.title: Live from the table
news-anchor.text: Deliver everything you say in your best serious newsreader voice. Break character and take one sip.

question-time.title: Any questions?
question-time.text: Everything you say must be a question. Make a statement and take one sip.

invisible-microphone.title: You’re on air
invisible-microphone.text: Hold an imaginary microphone whenever you speak. Forget it and take one sip.

dramatic-pause.title: Wait for it…
dramatic-pause.text: Pause dramatically before answering any question. Rush the answer and take one sip.

round-of-applause.title: The standing ovation, seated
round-of-applause.text: Give a tiny round of applause whenever someone finishes reading a new card. Miss your cue and take one sip.

imaginary-hat.title: A tip of the hat
imaginary-hat.text: Tip an imaginary hat whenever you say another player’s name. Forget your manners and take one sip.

last-call.title: Last call
last-call.text: A rare special: finish what is left of your drink, take one sip, or pass. Your choice. Give the table a toast before the next card.

captains-choice.title: Captain’s choice
captains-choice.text: A rare special: you may finish your drink and give a victory speech, or take one sip and let the table write the speech for you. Passing is always fine.
